raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38167.

When a diffusion forward fails with a CUDA error other than OOM (a driver error, a device-side assert, a caching-allocator assert), the device or its allocator can no longer be trusted. The worker logged the error, called `empty_cache()` and kept serving. So every later request either ran on the broken device or failed, and `/health` still returned `{"status": "ok"}`, which means no orchestrator would restart the server.

In #38167 the trigger is PyTorch's expandable-segments allocator: when a driver call fails with a non-OOM status during `ExpandableSegment::map()`, the half-created handles are not released, and every later allocation into that range hits `!handles_.at(i) INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED` (pytorch/pytorch#188008, pytorch/pytorch#166234; the report is on WSL2 with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`). That needs a PyTorch fix. This PR makes the server fail cleanly instead of staying up broken.

## Modifications

- `gpu_worker.py`: classify forward errors that leave the device unusable (`torch.AcceleratorError`, `CUDA driver error:`, `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:`, caching-allocator asserts, also through `__cause__`/`__context__`; anything mentioning "out of memory" is excluded). On the first one, record it, log the restart guidance (with the expandable-segments note), set `OutputBatch.device_unrecoverable`, and skip `empty_cache()`, which raised again from inside the error handler on a broken device. OOM keeps its current recover-and-continue behavior.
- `scheduler.py`: once the worker is flagged, `_handle_generation` rejects generation requests with "Device is in an unrecoverable state after an earlier error (...); restart the server." without running a forward (one reply per request, one per request group). The two dynamic-batch error paths carry the flag through.
- `scheduler_client.py` / `http_server.py`: the async client records the first flagged reply, and `/health` returns 503 `{"status": "unhealthy", "error": ...}` from then on. `/liveness` is unchanged.
- `schedule_batch.py`: new `OutputBatch.device_unrecoverable` field.

Not changed: an over-budget request still fails. It now fails without taking the server down silently. With DP > 1, `/health` goes 503 when any replica is flagged. With multi-rank TP/SP, each rank tracks its own state, so a rank that did not see the error behaves as before.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. Successful requests take the same path as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. The only added work on a successful request is one attribute check.

## Test environment

- GPU: 1x NVIDIA L40 (48 GB, sm_89), driver 610.43.02
- Host: cloud container, 6 vCPU (AMD EPYC 7773X), 48 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 6.17
- Software: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0 (nvcc 13.0.88), sglang-kernel 0.4.10, diffusers 0.37.0
- Base: upstream `main` at 0dc6de2e74

The unit tests are CPU-only; the GPU was used for the real CUDA error checks and the live server run below.

## Tests

- New `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_unrecoverable_device_error.py` (CPU, 14 cases): classifier on the two error strings from #38167 verbatim, a wrapped cause chain, OOM and an ordinary request error (negative branch); worker error path (flag set and `empty_cache()` skipped on a driver error, OOM unaffected); scheduler rejection without a forward; client plus `/health` 503, and still 200 after an ordinary error. All 14 fail with the source changes reverted.
- 32 existing unit files touching the scheduler, worker, client and HTTP server: 712 passed, 1 skipped (two `SimpleNamespace` worker stubs in `test_async_output_save.py` gained the new field).
- Real CUDA errors on an L40 (torch 2.14.1): a real allocation OOM is classified recoverable, a real device-side assert unrecoverable.
- Live server, L40, `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers` with default serve flags (as in CI), with a temporary uncommitted hook that makes one request perform an out-of-bounds GPU write:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| normal request | 200 | 200 |
| request that triggers the device-side assert | 500 | 500 |
| `/health` afterwards | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` | 503 with the CUDA error |
| next normal request | forward runs on the broken device, fails | rejected in 5 ms with the restart message |
| extra "scheduler event loop" error from `empty_cache()` | every failed request | none |

The WSL2 / 12 GB trigger from the report was not reproduced here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""A forward error that breaks the device must not leave the server serving.
+
+After a non-OOM CUDA driver error (sgl-project/sglang#38167), every later request
+either ran 5x slower or failed on a caching-allocator assert, while /health kept
+reporting ok. Such an error now rejects later requests and turns /health 503.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import pickle
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints import http_server
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers import gpu_worker as gpu_worker_module
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.gpu_worker import (
+    GPUWorker,
+    _is_unrecoverable_device_error,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.pipelines_core.schedule_batch import OutputBatch
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.scheduler_client import AsyncSchedulerClient
+
+# the two errors reported in #38167, verbatim
+_DRIVER_ERROR = "CUDA driver error: device not ready"
+_ALLOCATOR_ASSERT = (
+    '!handles_.at(i) INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/__w/pytorch/pytorch/c10/cuda/'
+    'CUDACachingAllocator.cpp":467, please report a bug to PyTorch.'
+)
+
+
+def _wrapped(message: str) -> Exception:
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise RuntimeError(message)
+        except RuntimeError as cause:
+            raise ValueError("stage failed") from cause
+    except ValueError as error:
+        return error
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error",
+    [
+        RuntimeError(_DRIVER_ERROR),
+        RuntimeError(_ALLOCATOR_ASSERT),
+        RuntimeError("CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered"),
+        _wrapped(_DRIVER_ERROR),
+    ],
+)
+def test_device_breaking_errors_are_unrecoverable(error):
+    assert _is_unrecoverable_device_error(error)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error",
+    [
+        torch.OutOfMemoryError("CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB"),
+        RuntimeError("CUDA error: out of memory"),
+        ValueError("height must be divisible by 16"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_oom_and_request_errors_stay_recoverable(error):
+    assert not _is_unrecoverable_device_error(error)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def worker(monkeypatch):
+    device = SimpleNamespace(reset_peak_memory_stats=Mock(), empty_cache=Mock())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_worker_module.torch, "get_device_module", lambda: device)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        type(gpu_worker_module.current_platform), "is_cpu", lambda self: False
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        type(gpu_worker_module.current_platform), "is_mps", lambda self: False
+    )
+    worker = GPUWorker.__new__(GPUWorker)
+    worker.is_output_rank = True
+    worker.server_args = SimpleNamespace(
+        pipeline_config=SimpleNamespace(supports_auto_residency=False)
+    )
+    worker._realtime_sessions = SimpleNamespace(attach=lambda req: None)
+    worker._release_warmup_pool = lambda req: None
+    worker._record_output_peak_memory = lambda *args, **kwargs: None
+    return worker, device
+
+
+def _forward_raising(worker, error):
+    req = SimpleNamespace(
+        request_id="req",
+        is_warmup=False,
+        extra={},
+        metrics=None,
+        trace_ctx=MagicMock(),
+        log=lambda **kwargs: None,
+    )
+
+    def forward():
+        raise error
+
+    return worker._execute_forward_common(
+        req,
+        forward_fn=forward,
+        log_reqs=[req],
+        return_req=False,
+        save_output_paths=lambda output_batch: None,
+        error_context="request req",
+    )
+
+
+def test_driver_error_marks_the_worker_and_skips_empty_cache(worker):
+    worker, device = worker
+
+    output = _forward_raising(worker, RuntimeError(_DRIVER_ERROR))
+
+    assert output.device_unrecoverable
+    assert _DRIVER_ERROR in worker.unrecoverable_device_error
+    # empty_cache on a broken allocator can raise out of the error handler
+    device.empty_cache.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_oom_keeps_the_worker_serving(worker):
+    worker, device = worker
+
+    output = _forward_raising(worker, torch.OutOfMemoryError("CUDA out of memory"))
+
+    assert not output.device_unrecoverable
+    assert worker.unrecoverable_device_error is None
+    device.empty_cache.assert_called_once_with()
+
+
+def _scheduler(unrecoverable_device_error):
+    scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler._async_output_save = False
+    scheduler.worker = SimpleNamespace(
+        is_sleeping=lambda: False,
+        unrecoverable_device_error=unrecoverable_device_error,
+        execute_forward=Mock(return_value=OutputBatch()),
+    )
+    return scheduler
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 3])
+def test_scheduler_rejects_generation_without_forward(num_reqs):
+    scheduler = _scheduler(f"request earlier: {_DRIVER_ERROR}")
+    reqs = [SimpleNamespace(is_warmup=False) for _ in range(num_reqs)]
+
+    result = scheduler._handle_generation(reqs, allow_dynamic_batching=True)
+
+    outputs = result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]
+    assert len(outputs) == num_reqs
+    for output in outputs:
+        assert output.device_unrecoverable
+        assert _DRIVER_ERROR in output.error
+        assert "restart the server" in output.error
+    scheduler.worker.execute_forward.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_rejected_request_group_gets_one_reply():
+    scheduler = _scheduler(f"request earlier: {_DRIVER_ERROR}")
+    group = [SimpleNamespace(is_warmup=False) for _ in range(2)]
+
+    result = scheduler._handle_generation(group, allow_dynamic_batching=False)
+
+    assert isinstance(result, OutputBatch)
+    assert result.device_unrecoverable
+

+def _client_replying(reply):
+    socket = MagicMock()
+    socket.send = AsyncMock()
+    socket.recv = AsyncMock(return_value=pickle.dumps(reply))
+    client = AsyncSchedulerClient()
+    client.context = SimpleNamespace(socket=lambda _socket_type: socket)
+    client.server_args = SimpleNamespace(
+        scheduler_rpc_timeout=None, scheduler_endpoints=["tcp://scheduler"]
+    )
+    client.request_logger = MagicMock()
+    return client
+
+
+def _health_status(client, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(http_server, "async_scheduler_client", client)
+    warmup_done = asyncio.Event()
+    warmup_done.set()
+    request = SimpleNamespace(
+        app=SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(server_warmup_done=warmup_done))
+    )
+    response = asyncio.run(http_server.health(request))
+    return 200 if isinstance(response, dict) else response.status_code
+
+
+def test_unrecoverable_reply_turns_health_unhealthy(monkeypatch):
+    error = f"Error executing request req: {_DRIVER_ERROR}"
+    client = _client_replying(OutputBatch(error=error, device_unrecoverable=True))
+
+    asyncio.run(client.forward(object()))
+
+    assert client.unrecoverable_device_error == error
+    assert _health_status(client, monkeypatch) == 503
+
+
+def test_ordinary_request_error_keeps_health_ok(monkeypatch):
+    client = _client_replying(OutputBatch(error="height must be divisible by 16"))
+
+    asyncio.run(client.forward(object()))
+
+    assert client.unrecoverable_device_error is None
+    assert _health_status(client, monkeypatch) == 200
